dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation

evidence.note: Systematic up-front orientation: enumerates all crates/src stubs/tests, reads Cargo.tomls (19-22), and greps the whole test corpus for cross-crate type/module usages (23-25) — maps the entire API surface and dependency order before coding, exceeding anchor 5's per-crate skim.

The ONLY consultation of /opt/k8s-reference is a single `find -maxdepth 2 -type d` directory listing; no upstream source file is ever read for semantics. The reference (source of truth) is effectively ignored — the gap that keeps this below anchor 8.

Deep, targeted contract reconstruction from test fixtures for scheduler affinity, ResourceQuota, watch events, finalizers, auth, DRA, admission webhooks — grounding each crate in its tests, but purely fixture-driven rather than reference-driven.

Re-greps tests to resolve specific field names (fully_labeled_replicas, CSR conditions, protobuf encoding) when new behaviors surface, consistently going back to tests — never to the upstream reference.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent mines tests, stubs, and manifests systematically and up front, mapping the full cross-crate API surface and dependency order and continually re-consulting tests as behaviors surface — clearly above anchor 5's per-crate test reading on the fixture half. But it consults the upstream reference exactly once and only to list directories, never reading any k8s source for semantics, and shows no distinction between fixture-visible contracts and hidden conformance requirements. Because anchor 8 demands mining tests AND the reference, the near-total absence of reference use caps this at 6: strong contract orientation from fixtures, weak reference grounding.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Front-loaded reconnaissance mapping crates, tests, Cargo.toml dependencies, and cross-crate use rusternetes_* references — establishing the dependency DAG before editing, a prerequisite for dependency-aware sequencing.

common (leaf) crate worked to green first: repeated cargo test -p rusternetes-common (--no-run then full) with fixes in between, treating 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check before advancing.
storage crate addressed only after common was green (cargo test -p rusternetes-storage), respecting leaf-first order — anchor-5 behavior.

api-server gated with repeated --no-run compile checks (116,145,149,170,196,200) interleaved with topical progression through handler families (watch, admission, rbac, proxy, dra), an implicit decomposition of the large crate into verifiable sub-units.

controller-manager work begins only after api-server, continuing the upward layering; but log ends here — scheduler/kubelet/proxy/kubectl/cloud/all-in-one milestones are never observed, and no explicit written exit-criteria plan for all ten crates appears.

dimensions.reasoning: Observed behavior cleanly matches anchor 5 — the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → controller-manager) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' gating each layer on the prior being green. It edges above 5 because the large api-server crate is decomposed into repeatedly compile-gated sub-units across handler families, but it falls short of anchor 8: there is no explicit dependency-aware milestone plan with declared exit criteria spanning all ten crates, and the sub-milestone progression looks reactive rather than pre-declared. This places the agent at a 6.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification

evidence.note: Per-crate compile-then-run loop on rusternetes-common: repeatedly builds tests with --no-run, runs cargo check, recompiles after edits, then actually runs the crate suite — a real incremental verify loop on the leaf crate.
Moves to storage crate with `cargo test -p rusternetes-storage --tests --no-run`, following leaf-to-root ordering, treating each crate's provided tests as the checkpoint.

Iterated `cargo test -p rusternetes-api-server --tests --no-run` runs interleaved with edit clusters — tight recompile cadence per fix, confirming the agent verifies as it goes rather than at the end.

No `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` runs, no prescribed thread/skip settings, and zero evidence of conformance reasoning (no booting the all-in-one binary, no HTTP/JSON semantic checks) — the bar stays at the green per-crate provided suite.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent runs each crate's provided tests as it goes with a disciplined compile(--no-run)-then-run loop, iterating per fix cluster in leaf-to-root order — squarely matching anchor 5's 'builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes.' It never reaches anchor 8: no workspace-wide --no-fail-fast runs, no prescribed thread/skip settings, no exact pass/fail tracking visible, and no deliberate reasoning about the hidden HTTP conformance suite or booting the all-in-one binary. Well above sporadic/end-only testing (3) but lacking the semantic/conformance layer, so 5.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking

evidence.note: Up-front scoping: enumerates crates, src/tests files, counts .rs files and reads manifests — establishes the shape of the horizon but produces no running tally of tests to pass.

Systematic per-crate build/test iteration in leaf-to-root order (common→storage→api-server), re-running cargo test after each patch batch — implicit per-crate pass/fail tracking and within-crate stuck-handling.
Repeated write_stdin steps indicate paging through test output (reading results), but no visible ledger, counts, or global done-vs-remaining accounting is recorded.
Trajectory ends mid controller-manager without ever reaching a workspace-wide test run or any tally across the 100-binary/1,390-test horizon; no regression-watch or loop-naming is observable.

dimensions.reasoning: Observable behavior shows disciplined per-crate iteration in dependency order with repeated re-testing after edits, i.e., a coarse per-crate pass/fail awareness and within-crate stuck-handling — consistent with the low end of anchor 5. But the log contains no concrete ledger of pass counts, no global done-vs-remaining accounting across the 100-binary horizon, and no visible regression detection or naming of circular debugging (anchor 8+ features). It sits above pure qualitative sense (3) but below full per-suite tracking, so 4. Confidence is low because the captured trajectory has no prose/observations and is truncated mid-task, making the assessment heavily inferential.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: cargo test on common reveals a failure; agent reads the specific failing test (ipaddress_test.rs), patches implementation, and re-tests — updating impl in response to test evidence (anchor-5 behavior).

api-server compile via --no-run; agent reads errors, greps for correct field/type names, applies a cluster of related patches, then recompiles — evidence-driven fixing of wrong inferred signatures/fields and adjusting nearby work.

greps LimitRange/verbs then serde_json usages and applies a series of related patches across the crate, correcting a systematic set of field/serialization mismatches rather than a single typo (slight lean above pure local fixing).
corrects field names (storage_class_name grep at 161), DRA handling, and recompiles — continued incremental correction of falsified field contracts.

further recompile/patch/protobuf cycles then proceeds to controller-manager; sequencing remains the originally planned leaf-to-root order — no forced resequencing or wholesale design abandonment observed.

dimensions.reasoning: Throughout the trajectory the agent responds to build/test evidence by reading the offending test, locating the wrong signature/field/semantic, patching, and re-verifying — and occasionally batches related fixes across a crate (steps 130-141), which is the core of anchor 5 ('updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work'). I found no clear instance of recognizing that a whole inferred contract or approach was wrong and backing it out, nor of reordering crates because a dependency proved blocking (anchor 8); the leaf-to-root plan holds unchanged. This places observed behavior at 5, with only a mild nudge toward 6 for systematic multi-patch corrections; confidence is medium because the log records only actions, not the errors or reasoning that drove them.

rubric.task_read: An extreme long-horizon software build: reimplement ten interdependent Kubernetes crates in Rust from stubs, with a load-bearing public API, 1,390 provided integration tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite demanding real k8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, tight cross-crate contracts inferred from tests + a pinned upstream reference, and the fact that passing visible fixtures is necessary but not sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing (leaf→root), incremental verification, and course-correction — meta-work here is decisive, not optional.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation
dimensions.description: Reading the tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, and the mounted v1.35 upstream reference to infer the exact API contracts and k8s semantics before and while implementing each crate.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (type names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key formats, watch/status semantics) is load-bearing and only partially discoverable from stubs; the hidden conformance suite punishes fixture-fitting. Acting without grounding each crate in the tests and the reference guarantees churn and shallow, non-conformant implementations.

anchors.0: Starts editing src stubs with no reading of the provided tests, manifests, or the /opt/k8s-reference tree; invents APIs.
anchors.3: Skims one crate's tests before coding it; ignores the upstream reference and the cross-crate dependency graph; repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures.
anchors.5: Reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing it, and consults the reference for the specific behaviors that crate is tested on; understands the workspace dependency order.
anchors.8: Systematically mines tests AND the upstream reference to reconstruct contracts (camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, watch semantics); maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front and notes where the hidden conformance suite implies behavior beyond the fixtures.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven investigation throughout: builds and continually refines an accurate model of k8s v1.35 semantics from the reference, proactively distinguishing test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, and re-consulting the reference whenever a new behavior surfaces rather than pattern-matching fixtures.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered set of milestones (respecting the dependency DAG, leaf crates first) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~1,390 tests across 100 binaries and strong inter-crate dependencies, order determines whether progress compounds or stalls; a downstream crate cannot be verified until its dependencies compile and pass. Milestone structure is the only way to keep a task this large tractable.

anchors.0: No plan; edits arbitrary crates in arbitrary order; attempts everything at once.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates'; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → …) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete exit criteria per crate, sub-milestones inside large crates (e.g. api-server: types→storage wiring→handlers→watches), and gating each layer on the prior layer being green.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences work to maximize compounding progress, isolates high-risk crates early, decomposes each large crate into independently verifiable units with crisp done-checks, and is continually re-ordered as dependency realities and test-failure clusters reveal the true critical path.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using cargo build/test per-crate and workspace-wide, plus reasoning about the hidden conformance suite, to confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is pass/fail on every non-skipped provided test AND a hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count. The agent must verify continuously against the provided suites while also engineering for real k8s semantics it cannot see — a verification challenge beyond just running the given tests.

anchors.0: Never builds or runs tests; declares crates done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test only sporadically or only at the very end, so failures pile up undiagnosed.
anchors.5: Builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and the workspace suite periodically, treating a green provided suite as the bar.
anchors.8: Tight verify loop per milestone (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts, and deliberately reasons about conformance behavior not covered by visible fixtures (booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics) so it doesn't just fixture-fit.
anchors.10: A rigorous, layered verification regime: fast per-unit checks feeding workspace-wide runs with the prescribed thread/skip settings, systematic triage of failure clusters, AND independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard the hidden conformance suite — catching over-fitting that would pass visible tests yet fail conformance.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which crates/tests pass vs. remain across ~1,390 tests, and detecting stuck/circular states rather than losing the plot.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The horizon is enormous; without an accurate running tally of done-vs-remaining and detection of thrashing (re-debugging the same crate, regressions in already-green crates), the agent will lose orientation, repeat work, or quit while wrongly believing it is close.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; cannot say which crates pass or how many tests remain.
anchors.3: Rough qualitative sense ('common seems done'); doesn't notice regressions or repeated failures.
anchors.5: Tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much of the suite is green; notices when a crate is stuck.
anchors.8: Maintains a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per test binary and remaining work, watches for regressions in previously-green crates after downstream edits, and flags when it is looping on the same failure.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the full 100-binary horizon: distinguishes real forward progress from churn, detects circular debugging early and names it, and reprioritizes based on where the largest verified gains remain — never mistaking local activity for global progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach, inferred contract, or crate ordering when build/test evidence contradicts expectations, instead of barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many contracts are inferred and will be wrong; some crates will prove harder or more entangled than expected. The ability to abandon a falsified API assumption or resequence when a dependency blocks progress is what separates sustained progress from thrashing on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach unchanged despite persistent errors; never revisits assumptions.
anchors.3: Makes only local patch-the-error fixes; doesn't reconsider a wrong contract or bad ordering even when failures cluster.
anchors.5: When a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic, updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work accordingly.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach or inferred contract is wrong (not just a typo), backs out and reworks it, and reorders remaining crates when a dependency proves blocking — citing the test/reference evidence that triggered the change.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven adaptation across the horizon: detects systemic mistakes early, cleanly abandons falsified designs before sinking more cost, revises the plan and re-verifies affected downstream crates, and consistently converts contradictory evidence into a better model rather than defending the original path.
